analysis.title: Early Morning Reid - Macro Strategy
key_insights: Markets face three overnight risks: AI growth concerns after Meta and Tesla earnings, higher oil on Middle East tensions, and French fiscal stress. S&P 500 closed +0.58% for a third straight gain, within 1% of its record high, but NASDAQ 100 futures are -1.32% and S&P 500 futures -0.66% this morning.

Brent crude is up about +1.73% to $110.70/bbl, near a five-month high. The NYT reported the US and Israel have drawn up plans for renewed strikes on Iran after the midterm elections, with targets likely including energy infrastructure.

Strikes on Saudi Arabia continued: two people were killed in an attack on the Shaybah oil field and another in a strike on King Fahd International Airport. The US State Department ordered non-emergency government staff and families out of Saudi Arabia.

Little sign of progress toward a US-Iran deal. Iran's foreign minister Araghchi wrote in an FT op-ed that Iran has no trust in the US administration's stated desire for peace and that there is little reason to expect progress now.
Oil markets price a longer period of high prices into 2027. The 12-month Brent future is +0.75% to $88.39/bbl.

Meta beat Q3 revenue ($64.6bn vs $63.3bn est.) and guided Q4 revenue to $73-76bn vs $73.6bn est. Shares rose more than 2% after hours. It raised the bottom of its 2026 capex range from $130-145bn to $135-145bn.

Tesla fell about 3% after hours after cutting its 2026 capex target from $25bn to $20bn, raising questions about the pace of its AI and robotics transition. Current revenue and earnings were close to expectations.

Asian equities fell: KOSPI -3.26%, Hang Seng -2.87%, Nikkei -2.00%, CSI 300 -1.26%, Shanghai Comp -0.89%. The CSI 300 briefly fell more than 20% from its June closing peak (bear market territory) before paring losses.
US equities rose before the Meta and Tesla results, led by tech. SpaceX earnings helped. The Philly semiconductor index rose 1.97% and the NASDAQ 1.05%. The STOXX 600 rose 0.92%, also led by tech.

France's 10yr yield rose 8.3bps to 5.01%, the first close above 5% since 2002. The Franco-German 10yr spread widened to 159bps, the highest close since 2011. The Euro crisis peak was 189bps in November 2011.
Spreads over bunds widened elsewhere: Italy +3.8bps to 116bps, and Spain +3.1bps to 66bps, its widest since June 2025.

Euro inflation pricing rose with energy. European gas futures rose 2.78% to €87.43/MWh and the 1yr Euro inflation swap rose 3.5bps to 3.82%, the highest since May. ECB hikes priced by the June 2027 meeting rose 2.0bps to 64bps.
US 10yr yield rose 1.1bps to 5.12% yesterday, then fell 3.5bps to 5.08% overnight on risk-off. The 30yr yield fell 3.1bps to 5.38%, which would be its lowest close in a month.

UK September CPI rose to 3.5% (vs 3.4% expected), the highest headline in nearly a year. Core CPI hit a 6-month high of 2.8%, in line with expectations. Markets price a 98% chance of a BoE hike in November.

The Bank of Korea held its rate at 3% as expected, said growth would be considerably higher than its August projections, and Governor Shin said it needs to maintain a tightening stance. New Zealand Q3 inflation was 3.7% y/y vs 3.8% expected.

earnings_insights: Meta Q3 revenue reported $64.6bn vs $63.3bn consensus est. Q4 revenue guidance $73-76bn vs $73.6bn est. 2026 capex plan raised to $135-145bn from $130-145bn. Shares +2% after hours.
Tesla cut 2026 capex target to $20bn from $25bn. Current revenue and earnings were close to expectations. Shares -3% after hours.
SpaceX earnings, released after the previous day's close, helped reassure investors that the tech rally was durable, and AI-exposed names did well.
